TRAINING: A typical training day for me would be double sessions, usually six days a week, with strength and conditioning three days a week in the mornings. Other than that, I am doing Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Muay Thai, MMA, wrestling, etc. each day.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I worked at a passport center doing monotonous work and I wanted to do something exciting, so I found martial arts about 10 years ago. 

What ranks and titles have you held? BJJ black belt, NEF lightweight champion

Do you have any heroes? In MMA, Carlos Condit.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means a lot. It's an accumulation of a lot of hard work. A lot of years of double training sessions and sacrificing time with family and it's great to finally see it pay off. It's nice to be able to show the world everything that I have been working so hard for the past several years.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went for one year, but realized it was not something that I cared to pursue. 

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked at the national passport center for seven and a half years, the entire time I have been training, and I was finally able to open my own academy about three years ago and train full time. I am also the head BJJ instructor for St. John’s Preparatory School in Danvers, MA.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I was the No. 1-ranked 155er in the northeast before going pro. I won Submission and Knockout of the Night awards as well.

Favorite grappling technique: Rock bottom

Favorite Striking technique: Ultimate punch

TRAINING: Wake up, morning practice at 9, train till 1 or 2, then go to strength and performance. Train for an hour, rest for 3 hours, then back to training at 5:30. I don’t leave the gym until 9 or so.
When and why did you start training for fighting? I wanted to start fighting since I was 14. I remember watching PRIDE re-runs with my older brother. I saw Quinton “Rampage” Jackson slam a guy and KO him. After that I wanted to fight.
What ranks and titles have you held? I have an amateur title at 155 and I have the V3 and Iron Tiger Series titles.
What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It would mean everything. It would mean I’m turning dreams into reality, and when I get this contract it’s only the beginning for me.
Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to school to become an engineer but I found out that wasn’t my calling.
What was your job before you started fighting? I was a CDL holder, so I drove semi trucks that carried construction material around Ohio, but I had to take the material off the truck manually. I carried dry wall, mud, steel, ceiling tiles, concrete, etc. up and down stairs. Then after a 10-12 hr shift I would go to practice.
Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I was 7-2-1 as an amateur - all finishes

What was your job before you started fighting? I used to mix and pour concrete. There were no machines in Brazil to do this.

Favorite grappling technique: Sweeps

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started at five years old in BJJ because my dad and my brother were involved in the sport. At 17 I did my first MMA fight in my hometown of Amazonas. Since then, I haven’t stopped, and that’s why I’m here now.

Who are your main training partners? Alessandro Costa, Austin bashi and Jake Hamiti.

What professional titles have you had? Champion of 3 regional promotions in Mexico: JFL MMA, XFL MMA, Lux Fight League.

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? Definitely the fight against Movsar Evloev. That fight made me known worldwide, because I was a nobody when I accepted the fight. And then my fight against Sabatini, where we fought in a big arena like Madison Square Garden.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It’s been my dream since watching the first UFC fighter, Zhang Tie Quan, fighting in UFC and even more after Zhang Wei Li won her championship. 

When and why did you start training to fight? I started training in Sanda as a teenager and have fought many kickboxing events before switching to MMA. 

Specific accomplishments in Pro competition? JCK championship, WLF championship

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career? My upcoming fight is my key fight. Getting into the UFC is a big deal and I have to win this, as many people are going to be watching especially since this show is in Macau, China. For past fights have to say the fight against Huysenov in A1 was a crucial fight for me to show the American audience that I am an exciting fighter.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Tough question as there are so many talented fighters. Israel Adesanya, I have watched Israel fight in many events in China and he puts up a very good fight.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? Bruce Lee

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? I have been helping my coach Bill Eng with Chinatown Overwatch (non-profit) and helping the Asian community in LA. I would like to see more young people learning about their culture, heritage, learning martial arts and empowering themselves. 

Beyond a championship and money, what motivates you? Being able to do my best, learning every day to improve my skills. 

Did you go to college, if so what degree did you earn? I was enrolled in the Xian Petroleum University and stopped to continue my career in MMA. 

Favorite Grappling Technique: D’arce Choke 

Favorite Striking Technique: The Sanda sidekick. It’s a very common technique where I am able to kick an opponent starting from about 10 feet away.

  • Wrestled under Erik Simmons - D1 Wrestler from the United States
  • Australian Amatuer MMA Champion
  • Pan-Pacific BJJ Gold Medalist
  • Was winning black belt divisions as a purple belt

Yuji (round 1 RTU) - I was a massive underdog with a far from perfect camp and still took out what many had picked as the #1 seed. qna.value:
TRAINING: Hit pads, do a technical class (whether it's Jiu-Jitsu; all around MMA training or weight training).

When and why did you start training for fighting? In 2010 I started training. It was a pact that my brother and I made to each other, to help him lose weight and to get my life on track. I also put fighting on my bucket list and said to myself (after watching UFC on TV), "I'm going to do that at least one time in my life (along with skydiving and deep-sea diving).

What ranks and titles have you held? None

Do you have any heroes? My Mother

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? All the hard work has got me here and now I have the chance to show the world that a dream can become your reality if you NEVER quit.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes, I studied psychology and criminal justice, but I have not achieved a degree in either yet.

What was your job before you started fighting? I was a MHT (Mental Health Tech) in a psych hospital.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? 135 lbs Tuff-n-Uff champion

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Fought for two world titles (short notice) and was never finished, fought all five rounds, one at 125 lbs (against a current UFC fighter) and one at 135 lbs

Favorite grappling technique: Jiu-Jitsu

Favorite Striking technique: Boxing
